# Military aviation and air defence (`military_aviation`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/military.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Warfare, security & deterrence (`military`)
- Deps: helped by glider_aeroplane, hot_air_hydrogen_balloon, radar, electromagnetic_waves_radio, internal_combustion_engine
- Core idea: Aircraft first of all see: reconnaissance and artillery spotting can reveal preparations on the ground. To deny the enemy that view one must control the air, which produced the fighter. Bombers attack armies, ships, transport and industry; aircraft from carriers replaced the battleship's guns. Defence against air attack is a system and not only an aeroplane: early warning (including British radar stations before 1940), a central plotting room and radio control of fighters. Bombing of cities proved far less decisive and far more costly than its prophets claimed.
- Pitfalls:
  - Douhet's prediction that bombing cities would quickly break civilian morale and end wars was wrong in 1940–1945
  - 'The bomber will always get through' ignored radar and fighters
  - Level bombing from height was grossly inaccurate until late in the Second World War
  - Air power needs airfields, fuel, spares and trained crews in depth; aircraft numbers alone mislead
- History: china: ancient to medieval – kites used for signalling and measuring distance in war; europe: 1794 – French observation balloon at Fleurus; 1911 – Italian aircraft reconnoitre and drop bombs in Libya; 1914–1918 – reconnaissance, fighters, bombers; 1921 – Douhet, Il dominio dell'aria; 1940 – Battle of Britain, radar-directed air defence; east_asia: 1941 – Japanese carrier strike on Pearl Harbor; americas: 1942 – Midway, a fleet battle in which US carrier aircraft sank four Japanese carriers; Japanese submarine I-168 torpedoed Yorktown and sank Hammann
- Read:
  - Giulio Douhet, Il dominio dell'aria (1921; English The Command of the Air, 1942)
  - Richard Overy, The Bombing War: Europe 1939–1945 (2013)
  - John Buckley, Air Power in the Age of Total War (1999)
